newsitem.title: MEXICO: Five killed in clashes between Mexican army, rebels.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in clashes between Mexican army, rebels.

text.p: Five people were killed on Tuesday in two clashes between the Mexican army and rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) in the southwestern state of Guerrero, officials said.

Mexico's military said three soldiers and two unidentified gunmen were killed in the incidents, which took place in the municipality of Atoyac de Alvarez, some 40 miles (62 km) northwest of this Pacific tourist resort.
A military official in Guerrero, who wished to remain anonymous, told Reuters the gunmen were identified as members of the Marxist EPR, which first appeared in this area in June 1996.
He also said at least 10 other soldiers were wounded in the attacks.

If confirmed, the attack would mark the second battle between the EPR and the army in the past week. Last weekend, two soldiers and two rebels died in a gunfight in Guerrero, one of Mexico's most impoverished states.
Mexico's army said the first of Tuesday's battles took place as soldiers were carrying out routine anti-drug operations in the region.
One soldier, Abad Noyola Calderon, was killed during an attack by 25 unidentified gunmen early in the afternoon, the military said.
Hours later, another battle erupted while soldiers were removing Noyola's corpse. It claimed the lives of two more soldiers and two gunmen, the military said.
"During the removal of the corpse of the soldier, carried out according to law, the attacks by the aggresors continued," the statement said.
"As a result, the troops responded and Lt. Angel Rios Reyes and Sgt. Javier Alvarez Rojas were killed. Also found were the bodies of two of the attackers," it added.
The Guerrero military official told Reuters the two dead gunmen were found wearing uniforms of the EPR and carrying AK-47 automatic rifles.
He said the wounded soldiers were taken to a military hospital in Acapulco.
After the first attack, three helicopters and two small aircraft flew over the area in search of the assailants. Some residents reported hearing an exchange of gunfire.
"We were prohibited from leaving our homes and we heard volleys of gunfire," Roberto Hernandez, a local teacher, told Reuters in a telephone interview from the nearby community of El Quemado.

The marxist rebels, who have called for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo's government, launched a series of attacks last year that killed about 30 people. They had been relatively quiet this year -- focusing on what they called "armed propaganda" to build support.

But the rebel group recently accused the military of waging a brutal counter-insurgency campaign and warned that it would renew attacks if the government did not stop hunting down the rebels and their sympathisers.
